text:
The candidate hypothesis posits a framework focused on the moderating effects of urban infrastructure quality, green technology integration, human capital, spatial compactness, and structural equation modeling (SEM) over the period 1990–2019. 

In contrast, the provided study uses annual data from 1960 to 2019 and employs Quantile Regression and spectral Granger-causality tests to investigate the direct relationships among ecological footprint, electricity consumption, GDP, trade openness, urbanization, and life expectancy. The candidate hypothesis introduces unrelated constructs, variables, and methodologies not supported or evaluated by the study.

VERDICT: REJECT
